next_question: Does the HTTP fingerprint substrate discriminate when response bodies and status codes are identical but server-side state changes only independent headers (e.g., Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie) — isolating header-only drift from body/status confounds?
why_next: The current experiment demonstrates discrimination on maximally-distinct writable controls (status+body change simultaneously), but C4 is vacuous (full==body==status==1.0) and cannot support the claim that the full vector adds marginal value. The audit's V2 (ceiling effect) and V3 (header correlation via Content-Length) identify that header-independent drift is the critical untested condition for C-FRESHNESS (session/auth drift when response content is unchanged) and C-DELTA-REPAIR (perturbation measurement when only metadata varies). A header-only drift experiment where bodies and statuses are identical but server-side state changes ETag/Cache-Control/Set-Cookie would directly test whether the substrate can detect non-body/non-status state changes, which is the actual use case for freshness detection and delta repair.

established: HTTP fingerprint substrate (status + body bytes + filtered standard headers) deterministically discriminates maximally-distinct writable controls on localhost Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 + SQLite WAL: permission escalation (SQLite UPDATE users SET role='admin', 403 vs 200+admin dashboard, Jaccard 1.0, N=20 but 1 unique fingerprint per state) and session invalidation (SQLite DELETE sessions, 200 vs 401, Jaccard 1.0). Null control on auth-state drift (fresh vs near-expiry valid JWT, identical responses) discrimination 0.0, CI[0.0,0.0]. All five frozen decision-rule conditions C1-C5 pass (EXP-RUNTIME-35697043449, audit REVISE with producer_claim_supported=false but recomputed metrics match producer).

Server reads role from SQLite (not from JWT payload) on each request, making writable role changes observable via HTTP. Session validity checked via SQLite DELETE, making session invalidation observable.

Auth-state drift (fresh vs near-expiry JWT with identical claims) produces identical server responses because server validates expiry but ignores remaining-time difference while both tokens are valid.
unknown: Does the substrate discriminate when response bodies and status codes are identical but server-side state changes only independent headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie) — header-only drift (audit V3, result.json unresolved[1])
Does the substrate discriminate same-status body-only permission changes (e.g., 200 with reader vs admin body content) without status code change (audit V2, result.json unresolved[3])

Does discrimination hold on production middleware (Django, Express, FastAPI) with realistic response variation (ETag, Cache-Control, Set-Cookie, non-deterministic Date/X-Request-Id) (audit V4, result.json unresolved[1])
Does the substrate discriminate under partial body overlap, concurrent load, HTTP/2, TLS, or multi-client scenarios (result.json unresolved[3-5])
Does N=20 suffice for non-degenerate bootstrap CI when responses have non-deterministic elements — current CI is degenerate due to deterministic responses (audit V1, result.json unresolved[5])
do_not_assume: C-MEAS-VALID is ready for VALIDATED or PRODUCT_CORE promotion — the audit REVISE status, vacuous C4, degenerate bootstrap CI, and untested header-only drift prevent advancement beyond EXPERIMENTAL

The full-vector fingerprint adds marginal value beyond single-field baselines — C4 is vacuous (1.0>=1.0 equality) because status and body change simultaneously on both positive conditions; body alone already achieves perfect discrimination

C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR are unblocked for distributed/production testing — this experiment demonstrates only localhost synthetic measurement substrate; production middleware, CDN, and distributed infrastructure are untested

Localhost Flask dev server results generalize to production WSGI/nginx — Flask development server (Werkzeug) on 127.0.0.1:19847 produces deterministic static JSON with no dynamic fields, no concurrency, no TLS/HTTP/2, no ETag/Cache-Control/Set-Cookie variation (audit V4)

Bootstrap CI [1.0,1.0] or [0.0,0.0] reflects sampling precision — CI is degenerate because all 20 fingerprints within each state are byte-identical (effective N=1, not 20); jitter 50-150ms has no observable effect on deterministic responses (audit V1)

B-HEADERS-ONLY discrimination 1.0 demonstrates independent header signal — headers are body-correlated via Content-Length (22 vs 108, 57 vs 28 bytes); no independent header-only variation tested (audit V3)

Null control validates header-only drift detection — null tests identical-code-path responses (fresh vs near-expiry JWT, same status+body+headers); header-only drift where bodies identical but headers vary is a separate untested condition

dependencies: Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 + SQLite 3.45.0 on localhost 127.0.0.1:19847 (Werkzeug dev server)
Same HTTP fingerprint computation: hash(status + body_bytes + sorted_filtered_headers) with EXCLUDED_HEADERS = [Date, Server, X-Request-Id]
Same seed (SEED=44) and jitter (50-150ms uniform) for reproducibility
SQLite-backed role lookup (role not in JWT payload) and session validity via DELETE

recommended_action: Design and execute a header-only drift experiment on the same Flask+SQLite+JWT localhost testbed where: (1) bodies and status codes are identical across conditions (same 200 + same JSON body); (2) server-side state changes only independent headers (e.g., Cache-Control max-age changes from 3600 to 0 after session metadata update, or ETag changes after data modification, or Set-Cookie is added/removed); (3) B-HEADERS-ONLY baseline should achieve discrimination > 0.0 while B-STATUS-ONLY and B-BODY-ONLY achieve 0.0; (4) full-vector discrimination should exceed B-BODY-ONLY (the first non-vacuous C4 test). This directly addresses audit V2 (ceiling effect), V3 (header correlation), and the C-FRESHNESS/C-DELTA-REPAIR use case of detecting state changes when response content is unchanged.
